title: Non-Alignment: From Compulsion to Strategic Autonomy

scenes.text: Was non-alignment India's moral choice or a desperate geopolitical compulsion?
scenes.narration: Imagine the world split into two rival camps, and everyone demands you pick a side. Nehru refused, arguing that non-alignment meant principled distance—judging every issue on right versus wrong rather than blind loyalty.

scenes.text: Judging every school dispute on its merits rather than joining rival campus gangs.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy: imagine two feuding groups of classmates bullying you to join them. Instead of picking a side or ignoring everyone, you decide each dispute fairly on its merits.

scenes.heading: Choice Or Compulsion
scenes.narration: Was this policy a noble choice or a survival compulsion? As a young democracy, India could not join the Soviets, yet joining the American bloc was dangerous with communist giants right on its border.

scenes.heading: Domestic Opinions Divided
scenes.narration: At home, leaders never fully agreed on this path. India's right wing favoured partnering with the West, while the left wing pushed for closer ties with Moscow.

scenes.name: C. Raja Mohan
scenes.idea: Non-alignment lacked domestic consensus and continues without any alternative grand idea.
scenes.narration: Here is the key insight from foreign policy scholar C. Raja Mohan. He notes that non-alignment was often elite rhetoric, surviving today simply because India has not invented a grand new idea.

scenes.heading: Evolution Of The Strategy
scenes.narration: Today, Indian leaders prefer the term strategic autonomy. Instead of rigid neutrality, the Non-Alignment 2.0 policy document recommends multiple alignment, letting India partner flexibly with several world powers.

items: Principled distance meant judging issues on right versus wrong.
Geopolitical necessity shaped policy rather than domestic consensus.
Modern strategy emphasizes strategic autonomy and multiple alignment.
scenes.narration: To recap, remember that non-alignment meant principled distance, began as a pragmatic compulsion rather than domestic consensus, and has transformed into strategic autonomy through multiple alignment.
